set.descent_text: After the chimney finish, scramble up and over slabs to an alpine lake, then hike back down into the grassy gully at the foot of the wall. The finish goes left and the belay is off the first good tree.

review.notes: Route page description.

set.descent_text: Walk across the landing to a large chockstone and belay from the tree anchor. Either rappel down the line of the climb or scramble off to one side or the other.

review.notes: Route page descent line.

set.descent_text: Descend by rappel from the rap anchors. The top belay at the handline ledge shares its anchor with a neighbouring route.

review.notes: Route page lists rap anchors and the shared top anchor.

set.descent_text: Rap anchors sit at both belays, the first on the belay ledge and the second at the top. Rappel from them to get down.

review.notes: Route page states rap anchors at both belay positions.

set.descent_text: The routes at this crag finish at bolted anchors, and bolted rappel stations serve the way down. An easy trail or scramble also reaches the top of the cliffs.

review.notes: Area-level statement about bolted anchors and rappel stations; route page gives no descent of its own.

set.descent_text: Finish at the bolted anchor. From there you can walk off, or rappel from the separate rap anchor to the left.

review.notes: Protection section of the route page.

review.notes: Route page: bolted anchors. Area page: all routes have bolted anchors and rappel stations; trail or scramble to the tops.

set.descent_text: Descend by rappel from the rap anchors at the top of the crack above the yew tree.

review.notes: Route page lists rap anchors.

set.descent_text: Descend by rappel from the rap anchors above the long runout to the top of the climb.

review.notes: Route page lists rap anchors.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes, from where the steep headwall ends; easier, lower-angle ground continues from there to the summit. Every pitch has a bolted anchor except the fourth, so note where the gear belays are on the way up.

review.notes: Route page: rappel from end of headwall, two 60 m ropes, bolted anchors on all but one pitch. Anchor beta may predate the page author last climbing it.

set.descent_text: The variation finishes on the Mighty Mouse anchors. From there, rappel Mighty Mouse with two ropes.

review.notes: Own page says to rappel Mighty Mouse; that page gives the two-rope requirement.

set.approach: From the Nesakwatch trailhead, follow the trail to a large granite wall, then go right and up into the basin below the spires. The route is on the left wall of North Nesakwatch Spire; a small tree with a thick trunk marks the end of the first pitch.

review.notes: Approach only; descent not stated.

set.approach: From the Nesakwatch trailhead, follow the trail to a large granite wall, then go right and up into the basin below the spires. The line is a lengthy, straight crack on the north flank of the west ridge of North Nesakwatch Spire.

review.notes: Approach only; descent not stated.

set.descent_text: Descend either by rappelling from a small tree or by walking off to the left.
set.approach: From the Nesakwatch trailhead, follow the trail to a large granite wall, then go right and up into the basin below the spires. The route is a single pitch near the col between the North and South Spires.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent and the col location; area page the trail approach.

set.descent_text: The last pitch goes around the summit smokestack to its east side and up a hand crack to the top. Descend by rappelling from slung blocks.

review.notes: Route page gives the top-out and the slung-block rappel.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes from the top of the pillar. Not every rappel anchor sits at a belay, so note them on the way up. Loose rock and snagged ropes are the hazards, the anchors may need fresh cord, and gear left on the big horn low on the route can be collected on the way down.

review.notes: Route page descent notes.

set.descent_text: The last pitch is fourth-class scrambling over loose blocks to the top of the tower. The belay anchors are bolted, so descend by rappelling the route. Some of the rappels are long enough that a tag line is needed.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Rappel the bolted stations down the pinnacle's west face using two ropes, after the final traverse right and the crack to the summit.

review.notes: Route page descent line.

set.descent_text: Every belay anchor is bolted and fitted with rappel hangers, so the route can be rappelled. The bolted anchor on the Gar ledge, at the top of the fourth pitch, is one of the stations. Take two ropes.

review.notes: Route page; two ropes from the same page rack note. Full rappel sequence not given.

set.descent_text: The route finishes by stemming to the top of Prince Albert Tower. The anchors are bolted, so rappel the route with two ropes.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The route ends at rap anchors; descend by rappel from them.

review.notes: Route page lists rap anchors.
